sources.title: GLM-5.3 | OpenLM.ai
sources.snippet: GLM-5.3 is our latest flagship model for coding and long-horizon tasks. It marks a substantial leap in long-horizon task capability over its predecessor GLM-5.1 and delivers that capability on a solid 1M-token context. It is pure open with an MIT open-source license — no regional limits, technical access without borders.

sources.title: GLM (AI) - Wikipedia
sources.snippet: Z.ai released GLM-5.3 on 14 August 2026 and made the model's weights available two weeks later. [9][10][11] Later that month, Z.ai anonymously previewed a model called Ox Alpha on OpenRouter, which was released with weights on 26 August as GLM-5.3-Flash.

sources.title: GLM 5.3: What's New, Benchmarks, and How to Access It (2026)
sources.snippet: What carried over from 5.2 Because the base model is unchanged, the spec sheet mostly reads like GLM 5.2's. Z.ai positions the 5.2 base around a usable 1M-token context, and 5.3 inherits that; a separate 5.3 model card with its own numbers hadn't been published at the time of writing, so treat context and parameter details as carried over rather than re-confirmed.
